name: SC-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+11 district with incumbent William Timmons renominated
Timmons holds a roughly 13-to-1 fundraising edge plus $487K in outside support
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 4 percent
No polls or expert ratings show any sign of a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's strong Republican lean, Timmons's incumbency, and his dominant fundraising position point to him holding the seat, and prediction markets agree at roughly a 4 percent Democratic chance. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting competitiveness, there is no evidence to move the forecast materially away from the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Timmons or a national environment even more favorable to Democrats than current fundamentals assume could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 4th District leans Republican by about eleven points, and incumbent William Timmons returns after winning renomination. He has raised roughly $1.8 million and benefits from about $487,000 in outside support, while Democrat Courtney McClain has raised about $131,000 with modest cash on hand. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but has raised under $1,000.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals and markets. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a four percent chance of an upset. The national environment is somewhat favorable to Democrats, but that is unlikely to overcome the district's lean, the incumbent's financial advantage, and the absence of any signs of a competitive race. Timmons is positioned to win another term, with the main question being the size of his margin.
